topics.title: Stern Discusses Bathroom Habits and Political Opinions
topics.summary: Howard Stern discusses his bathroom reading habits while expressing frustration with being unable to get a word in edgewise on air. He criticizes claims of America’s superiority over communist or Nazi regimes, makes comments about Mick Jagger's finances, and engages in playful banter with co-hosts.

topics.title: Itchy Man's Phone Call
topics.summary: Howard conducts a bizarre phone interview discussing his persistent itching and unusual remedies like suppositories recommended by a doctor. He engages in awkward conversations with Captain Jenks about Larry King’s bad breath and attempts to question police conduct, culminating in an uncomfortable moment when Larry begins shaving his head on air.

topics.title: Voice Box Experiments and a Caller's Plea
topics.summary: During an on-air experiment with voice modification devices – including one for individuals without larynxes – hosts Howard and Robin engage callers in conversations. They discuss potential users, the challenges of speech production, attempt a Cancer Man song using modified voices, and explore various device options while fielding calls about dating prospects.

topics.title: The Cancer Man Phone Call
topics.summary: A chaotic radio segment features callers discussing a mysterious individual nicknamed 'The Cancer Man,' who makes bizarre recordings filled with nonsensical phrases like ‘the cancer can cuss.’ The conversation quickly spirals into an awkward and confusing discussion involving Russian Jews, vibrators, speech therapy, and unsettling personal inquiries about relationships and sexual experiences.

topics.title: Stern Disputes Media Criticism & FCC Concerns
topics.summary: Howard Stern discusses negative reactions from listeners regarding his comments about Jim Kerr and expresses frustration with media portrayals of him as a ‘shock jock,’ particularly an article featuring himself. He dismisses accusations from David Hinkley, criticizes the Daily News’s perceived bias fueled by advertising interests, and reacts to FCC concerns over potential censorship related to his broadcast content.

topics.title: Nancy Reagan’s Lunch & Barbara Walters Gossip
topics.summary: During lunch with Nancy Reagan, conversations centered on Barbara Walters' recent invitation and Liz Smith’s interest. Concerns arose about Elaine’s attempts to influence the narrative through a Showtime special, while Howard expressed frustration over perceived media bias and accusations of falsehoods printed about him. The discussion also touched upon the FCC scrutiny and ongoing debates surrounding freedom of speech.
